intro: Lesson 8: How much chocolate? Treats and healthy food. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

blocks.title: Sort into: Everyday food / Treat (sometimes)
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Everyday food, Treat (sometimes).
blocks.answer: Everyday food: Apple; Rice; Carrot; Bread. Treat (sometimes): Chocolate bar; Crisps; Fizzy drink; Cake

box.title: Draw a balanced plate for lunch, with a small treat on the side.

keywords.def: a food for sometimes, not every day
a bit of each kind of food

questions.q: Is a big bag of sweets every day tayyib? Why?
questions.a: No: too much sugar is bad for our teeth and body.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: draw a balanced plate for lunch with a small treat on the side.
questions.a: A plate with fruit or vegetables, a starchy food, a protein and a small treat.

questions.q: Extend: say why we wash fruit before eating.
questions.a: To clean off dirt and germs.
A) Chocolate. Chocolate has lots of sugar: a sometimes food.

questions.q: Think again: Would it be good to eat chocolate for breakfast, lunch and dinner? Why or why not?
questions.a: No: it has lots of sugar and gives no balance. A small treat sometimes is fine; we need healthy foods most.
